findings.class: E-23 cluster warrant rests on an English-visible image field
findings.claim: The row's load-bearing binder, stated as the shared building-image vocabulary of house, established and rooms, is not a lexical sharing at all, because Prov.24.3 and Prov.24.4 share zero skeleton content tokens, and the rival single-proverb atomization is set aside on that same image ground.
findings.grounds: Re-derived at skeleton tier, the token sets of 24:3 and 24:4 intersect in the empty set; the three items the row names are בָּ֑יִת and יִתְכּוֹנָֽן, both inside 24:3, and חֲדָרִ֣ים in 24:4 -- three different lexemes standing in one image field that is fully visible in translation, not a repeated token or root, so the warrant is tier-4 topic affinity and cannot carry a cluster, and the confidence of high rests on it. The byte object that does bind the pair goes unnamed: the instrumental bet plus wisdom-triad series בְּ֭חָכְמָה and וּ֝בִתְבוּנָ֗ה in 24:3 continued by וּ֭בְדַעַת opening 24:4, a three-member colon-initial series whose members are the same triad that co-occurs at Prov.2.6 and that runs across a verse boundary in the same order at Prov.3.19 and Prov.3.20 (בְּחָכְמָ֥ה, בִּתְבוּנָֽה, בְּ֭דַעְתּוֹ) alongside כּוֹנֵ֥ן, the same root that 24:3 carries in יִתְכּוֹנָֽן. All quoted runs are byte tier, spliced from the staged verse map and re-collated at their cited refs; the zero-overlap result is skeleton tier. The span itself is not challenged by this finding: it survives on the unnamed series, so the repair is a warrant replacement.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the binder clause in boundary_rationale and the matching signal in observed_substrate_signals: name the instrumental bet plus wisdom-triad series (בְּ֭חָכְמָה and וּ֝בִתְבוּנָ֗ה at 24:3, וּ֭בְדַעַת opening 24:4) as the cohesion object at skeleton tier, state that 24:3 and 24:4 share zero skeleton content tokens so the pair is bound by the series rather than by a repeated lexeme, and drop house-established-rooms to a device_notes image note; the replacement passes the test that killed the original because its members are byte objects at named refs rather than glosses. strongest_rejected_alternative re-opens with it and must reject the atomization on the series rather than on the completed figure. Confidence may stay at high only on the replaced warrant. Proposal only; nothing is applied.

findings.class: cross-seam cohesion disclosed on one side only
findings.claim: The row makes no disclosure at its own closing edge, where the third member of the series it actually rests on has an immediate recurrence in the next verse, while the row on the other side of the same seam discloses that recurrence with digits.
findings.grounds: Both sides of the 24:4|24:5 seam, byte tier: 24:4 closes ה֖וֹן יָקָ֣ר וְנָעִֽים and 24:5 opens גֶּֽבֶר חָכָ֥ם בַּע֑וֹז and continues וְאִֽישׁ דַּ֝֗עַת. The deciding object is the instrumental bet plus wisdom-triad series, whose third member וּ֭בְדַעַת opens 24:4 and which has no member in 24:5, where the same noun stands as a construct nomen rather than a bet-prefixed instrumental; the wider instrumental-bet pattern is not bounded and does continue at 24:5 in בַּע֑וֹז and at 24:6 in בְ֭תַחְבֻּלוֹת and בְּרֹ֣ב, which is exactly why the triad and not the preposition is the bounding object. Re-swept at skeleton tier, the contiguous string for that third member stands at 44 of 915 verses and forms exactly 5 adjacent-verse pairs book-wide (Prov.2.5-Prov.2.6, Prov.8.9-Prov.8.10, Prov.14.6-Prov.14.7, Prov.22.19-Prov.22.20, Prov.24.4-Prov.24.5), so the recurrence is textural and carries no merge across this seam; the cure is disclosure, not respan.
findings.proposed_change: Add one clause to device_notes disclosing the recurrence across the closing edge with its swept digits (44 of 915 verses, 5 adjacent-verse pairs book-wide, this being one of them) and stating that the bet-plus-triad series is exhausted at 24:4 while the wider instrumental-bet pattern continues at 24:5 and 24:6; boundary_evidence_refs gains oshb:Prov.24.5. Span unchanged. Proposal only.

findings.class: form label falsified by the pointed bytes
findings.claim: The device_notes label of the second verb of 24:3 as a Niphal passive is falsified by the pointed bytes, which carry a prefixed tav that no Niphal imperfect of that root carries in this book.
findings.grounds: 24:3 reads וּ֝בִתְבוּנָ֗ה יִתְכּוֹנָֽן at byte tier; the Niphal imperfect of the same root is written אָדָ֣ם at Prov.12.3, בִ֝צְדָקָ֗ה at Prov.16.12, וְיִכּ֖וֹן at Prov.25.5 and יִכּֽוֹן at Prov.29.14, four verses at contiguous skeleton tier, none of them carrying the tav, while the form at 24:3 stands at exactly 1 verse book-wide. The staged extract has no morphology layer, so the class is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' passive renderings rather than machine-verified; the co-cited first verb is a Niphal, so only the second label is wrong, and the load-bearing point of the sentence -- third person, not a governing second-person imperative or vetitive -- is unaffected.
findings.proposed_change: In device_notes, drop the Niphal label from the second verb and describe the pair by what the bytes show: two third-person passive-sense forms, one Niphal and one tav-prefixed, neither a governing second-person imperative or vetitive. No other field changes. Proposal only.

findings.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative tests only the rival backward extension into the preceding cluster and never states the rival atomization of 24:5 and 24:6 as separate rows, which is the rival a cluster claim has to defeat.
findings.grounds: At skeleton tier 24:5 and 24:6 share zero content tokens, so the row's sole cohesion object is the verse-initial particle כִּ֣י opening 24:6, which the row states honestly as a motive-clause warrant rather than a repeated-vocabulary one; that makes the atomization the live rival, defeasible on bytes only by the syntactic dependency of the particle clause, which the row never argues. Both edges re-checked: 24:4|24:5 carries the recurrence the row itself discloses, and 24:6|24:7 shares zero skeleton tokens (24:6 closes בְּרֹ֣ב יוֹעֵֽץ, 24:7 opens רָאמ֣וֹת לֶֽאֱוִ֣יל חָכְמ֑וֹת), so no undisclosed device straddles the back edge. The row sits in the collection whose ruled operative category is admonition_unit and outside the owner-ruled atomic-default zone of 10:1-22:16 and 25-29, so the omission is a completeness shortfall rather than a substantive risk to the span.
findings.proposed_change: Add the mandated rival as the second sentence of strongest_rejected_alternative, within the ruled two-sentence shape: state the atomization of 24:5 and 24:6 as separate single_proverb rows and reject it on the byte ground that the second verse opens with a dependent motive particle and has no independent standing, noting that the two verses share zero skeleton content tokens. No other field changes. Proposal only.

findings.class: count object mislabelled as a root
findings.claim: The disclosure calls the recurring element a root and attaches the digit 44 of 915 verses, but 44 is the digit for a contiguous skeleton string that blends a noun with an infinitive construct, and the string is not the root.
findings.grounds: Both of the row's digits verify exactly: re-swept at skeleton tier the contiguous string stands at 44 of 915 verses with 46 token occurrences, and its adjacent-verse pairs are exactly 5 (Prov.2.5-Prov.2.6, Prov.8.9-Prov.8.10, Prov.14.6-Prov.14.7, Prov.22.19-Prov.22.20, Prov.24.4-Prov.24.5), so the row's 44 and its five-pairs claim are byte-true. What does not verify is the object label: the same sweep captures לָדַ֣עַת at Prov.1.2, an infinitive construct rather than the noun quoted at 24:4 and 24:5 (וּ֭בְדַעַת, דַּ֝֗עַת, byte tier), and the quoted noun is itself a formation of a different triliteral root, so the swept object is a spelling and the true root class is larger than 44. The count-object discipline requires the object to be named before the digit; the row's own conclusion that the recurrence is textural is strengthened, not weakened, by the correction.
findings.proposed_change: In device_notes, relabel the object: call it the contiguous skeleton string rather than the root, keep the verified digits (44 of 915 verses, 5 adjacent-verse pairs book-wide), and add that a root-scoped count would be larger still. No other field changes. Proposal only.

findings.claim: Two Hebrew splices are glossed beyond their own extent, one rendered as a man of schemes when the splice omits the construct head, the other rendered as a full nominal sentence when the splice omits the predicate.
findings.grounds: 24:8 reads ל֝֗וֹ בַּֽעַל מְזִמּ֥וֹת יִקְרָֽאוּ and 24:9 opens זִמַּ֣ת אִוֶּ֣לֶת חַטָּ֑את, both byte tier and re-collated at oshb:Prov.24.8 and oshb:Prov.24.9; the first gloss covers בַּֽעַל מְזִמּ֥וֹת while the splice is only מְזִמּ֥וֹת, and the second gloss covers זִמַּ֣ת אִוֶּ֣לֶת חַטָּ֑את while the splice is only זִמַּ֣ת אִוֶּ֣לֶת, so in both places the gloss extent exceeds the splice extent. The rule cures by re-cutting either side and touches no boundary, so the span, the unit_type and the confidence are unaffected.
findings.proposed_change: Re-cut for parity in boundary_rationale: either extend the splices to בַּֽעַל מְזִמּ֥וֹת and זִמַּ֣ת אִוֶּ֣לֶת חַטָּ֑את, or cut the glosses back to a man-of-schemes head-noun and to the scheme of folly. No other field changes. Proposal only.

findings.class: cohesion object carries no count object and no digit
findings.claim: The row's only cohesion object, the repeated scheme-root across its internal seam, is stated without a count object or a digit, so a reader cannot tell whether the root is bounded or pervasive.
findings.grounds: At skeleton tier 24:8 and 24:9 share no token, the two realizations being distinct strings, so the object is correctly tiered by the row as a consonantal-root match rather than a token match; re-swept, the contiguous skeleton string for that root stands at 13 of 915 verses (Prov.1.4, Prov.2.11, Prov.3.21, Prov.5.2, Prov.8.12, Prov.10.23, Prov.12.2, Prov.14.17, Prov.21.27, Prov.24.8, Prov.24.9, Prov.30.32, Prov.31.16) and Prov.24.8-Prov.24.9 is the ONLY adjacent-verse pair the class forms in the book, which is stronger evidence for this cluster than the row claims for itself. Both edges re-checked and clean: 24:7|24:8 and 24:9|24:10 share zero skeleton tokens (24:7 closes בַּ֝שַּׁ֗עַר לֹ֣א יִפְתַּח פִּֽיהוּ, 24:8 opens מְחַשֵּׁ֥ב לְהָרֵ֑עַ; 24:9 closes וְתוֹעֲבַ֖ת לְאָדָ֣ם לֵֽץ, 24:10 opens הִ֭תְרַפִּיתָ בְּי֥וֹם צָרָ֗ה), and the only cross-seam root recurrence in the neighbourhood, the folly root at 24:7 and 24:9, skips 24:8 and belongs to a class of 38 verses book-wide, so it carries no merge at the front edge.
findings.proposed_change: Add the digit and the object to device_notes or observed_substrate_signals: name the swept object as the contiguous skeleton string of the scheme-root, give 13 of 915 verses, and state that this is the class's only adjacent-verse pair in the book. No other field changes. Proposal only.

findings.class: cluster warrant not byte-grounded; the one spanning object unnamed
findings.claim: The three-verse cluster has no adjacent-pair lexical cohesion at either internal seam, and the single lexical object that does span it is never named, so the stated warrant is a functional reading of the material rather than a byte-grounded one.
findings.grounds: Skeleton-tier token sets: 24:23 and 24:24 intersect in the empty set, 24:24 and 24:25 intersect in the empty set, and 24:23 and 24:25 intersect in exactly one token, realized as בַּל טֽוֹב closing 24:23 and בִרְכַּת טֽוֹב closing 24:25, both byte tier and re-collated at their refs, with the token absent from 24:24. That object is positional -- span-initial verse and span-final verse, absent from the middle verse -- and not a bounded catchword: re-swept, the contiguous skeleton string stands at 63 of 915 verses, so it is weak positive evidence and must ship with that digit. The only other byte object the row names, the waw opening וְלַמּוֹכִיחִ֥ים יִנְעָ֑ם, binds 24:25 to 24:24 rather than to 24:23. The row's confidence of medium_low is calibrated to the thinness, but the warrant text is not.
findings.proposed_change: In boundary_rationale and observed_substrate_signals, name the spanning object (the token closing 24:23 in בַּל טֽוֹב and closing 24:25 in בִרְכַּת טֽוֹב, absent from 24:24) as a positional inclusio, qualify it with its swept digit of 63 of 915 verses, and state that neither internal seam carries a shared skeleton token; keep the confidence at medium_low. Proposal only.

findings.class: rival split live and undecided on bytes
findings.claim: The rival split of the header verse from the curse-and-blessing pair is set aside on a functional ground, and the forward-link test the corpus applies to the book's only other verse-initial gam-elleh header would leave this header free-standing too.
findings.grounds: Both sides of the proposed seam, byte tier: 24:23 closes הַֽכֵּר פָּנִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט בַּל טֽוֹב and 24:24 opens אֹ֤מֵ֨ר לְרָשָׁע֮ צַדִּ֪יק אָ֥תָּה, and the two verses share zero skeleton tokens. The devices that decide are (a) the verse-initial header formula גַּם אֵ֥לֶּה, one of exactly two verse-initial sites book-wide, the other being Prov.25.1, and (b) the waw of וְלַמּוֹכִיחִ֥ים binding 24:25 to 24:24. At the parallel site the shipped corpus rows Prov.25.1 free-standing on the stated ground that no adjacent-verse skeleton token links it forward, and 25:1 and 25:2 do indeed share none (25:1 closes אַנְשֵׁ֤י חִזְקִיָּ֬ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה, 25:2 opens כְּבֹ֣ד אֱ֭לֹהִים הַסְתֵּ֣ר דָּבָ֑ר); applied here the same test returns the same result, so the two gam-elleh headers are decided by different tests. Against the split stands only the positional inclusio at 24:23 and 24:25, whose token stands at 63 of 915 verses. I record the rival as live and undecided on the bytes and do not adjudicate it.
findings.proposed_change: Rival respan for owner triage, adopt only if the adjudicator judges the positional inclusio too weak to hold three verses: replace Prov.24.23-Prov.24.25 with two rows tiling the same range exactly -- first Prov.24.23-Prov.24.23, unit_type single_proverb, warranted by the verse-initial header formula גַּם אֵ֥לֶּה (2 of 2 verse-initial sites book-wide) plus the verse's own complete maxim, carrying the same header disclosure the corpus uses at Prov.25.1 because the closed vocabulary has no header value; second Prov.24.24-Prov.24.25, unit_type proverb_cluster, warranted by the waw of וְלַמּוֹכִיחִ֥ים binding the blessing colon to the curse case, with the one-sentence deviation disclosure that C4's operative categories are admonition_unit and single_proverb. Both rows keep parent_collection C4 Prov.24.23-Prov.24.34 and confidence medium_low; both must disclose that the inclusio token spanning 24:23 and 24:25 is severed by the split and that it stands at 63 of 915 verses. This is a proposal recorded for adjudication and is applied to nothing.

findings.class: missing deviation disclosure for a non-operative unit_type
findings.claim: The span is typed proverb_cluster inside a collection whose ruled operative categories are admonition_unit and single_proverb, without the one-sentence deviation disclosure the ratified amendment requires in device_notes.
findings.grounds: The amendment permits any value of the closed eight-value vocabulary inside any collection where the row's own bytes carry that form, on condition of a one-sentence deviation disclosure in device_notes; this row's device_notes carries a parallelism note and a confidence rationale and no deviation sentence, while the three sibling rows of this same slice in the adjoining collection each carry theirs. The bytes do support a non-admonition type here: 24:23's הַֽכֵּר פָּנִ֖ים stands as the subject of the not-good predicate בַּל טֽוֹב rather than as a governing command -- the pointed form belongs to a pattern that is homographic between a Hiphil imperative and a Hiphil infinitive absolute, the same pattern carrying a true imperative nearby at 24:11 in הַ֭צֵּל, so the form alone does not decide and the predicate does -- and 24:24 opens with the participial אֹ֤מֵ֨ר; the staged extract has no morphology layer, so this is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, and the repair is the missing sentence rather than a type change.
findings.proposed_change: Add one sentence to device_notes stating that the collection's operative categories are admonition_unit and single_proverb and that this span is typed proverb_cluster because its own bytes carry no governing second-person imperative or vetitive. No other field changes. Proposal only.

findings.claim: The setumah citation discloses type and single-witness at every layer but never names its tier or its corroboration-only status, which the standing rule requires whenever a non-textual signal is cited.
findings.grounds: The staged inventory carries Prov.24.22 as the book's only SAMEKH among 52 segs, 51 of them PE, so the row's type disclosure is correct, petuchah is not conflated with setumah, and single-witness is stated in the rationale, in the refs entry and in the signals; what is missing is the tier, parashah in the Writings being tier-3 weak corroboration and never a boundary driver, which the row on the other side of the same seam at Prov.24.21-Prov.24.22 does state. In substance the front edge is carried by the tier-1 verse-initial header formula גַּם אֵ֥לֶּה, so the mark is not doing driver work and the defect is the missing label; no paseq or ketiv/qere claim is made anywhere in the row, and the inventory shows no ketiv/qere note inside the span, so nothing else is owed.
findings.proposed_change: Add the tier label to the setumah citation in boundary_rationale and to the matching entry in observed_substrate_signals: tier-3 weak corroboration, single-witness, never a driver. No other field changes. Proposal only.

findings.claim: Two Hebrew splices are glossed beyond their own extent, the first rendered with a predicate the splice omits and the second rendered with a verb the splice omits.
findings.grounds: 24:23 reads הַֽכֵּר פָּנִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט בַּל טֽוֹב and 24:25 opens וְלַמּוֹכִיחִ֥ים יִנְעָ֑ם, both byte tier at their cited refs; the first gloss carries a not-good predicate while the splice stops at הַֽכֵּר פָּנִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט, and the second gloss carries a pleasantness verb while the splice is only וְלַמּוֹכִיחִ֥ים, so in both places the gloss extent exceeds the splice extent. The cure re-cuts one side or the other and touches no boundary.
findings.proposed_change: Re-cut for parity in boundary_rationale: extend the splices to הַֽכֵּר פָּנִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט בַּל טֽוֹב and וְלַמּוֹכִיחִ֥ים יִנְעָ֑ם, or cut the glosses back to match the shorter runs. No other field changes. Proposal only.

findings.class: digit scoped to a work unit; tooling narrated in row prose
findings.claim: The row's exclusivity digit is scoped to a writer part and narrated as a tool run, both of which are workflow language barred from row prose, leaving a reader of the corpus a digit that cannot be checked.
findings.grounds: The sentence naming a targeted sweep of this part's skeletons and 2 of the part's 83 verses names a work unit and a tool operation rather than a textual domain. Re-swept, the claim is true and can be stated in corpus terms: the contiguous skeleton string of the plural stands at 7 of 915 verses (Prov.8.15, Prov.16.12, Prov.16.13, Prov.22.29, Prov.25.2, Prov.25.3, Prov.31.4), of which exactly 2 fall inside Prov.25.1-Prov.27.27, and the singular is exhausted inside that range by the three sites the row names, Prov.25.1, Prov.25.5 and Prov.25.6, its contiguous skeleton string standing at 24 verses book-wide. The allography the sweep depends on is real and in the row's favour, since the final-letter singular is not a substring of the medial-letter plural, so the two objects cannot be blended by a contiguous sweep. The row's two cited splices are byte-identical at the two sites (מְ֝לָכִ֗ים at 25:2 and מְ֝לָכִ֗ים at 25:3, equal byte for byte) and the second shared token is an exact skeleton match realized as חֲקֹ֣ר and חֵֽקֶר, so the two-token claim across the seam verifies.
findings.proposed_change: Restate the digit in corpus terms in boundary_rationale and observed_substrate_signals: the plural stands at 7 of 915 verses book-wide and at 2 verses inside Prov.25.1-Prov.27.27, namely this row's two; drop the sweep narration and the work-unit scoping. No other field changes. Proposal only.

findings.claim: The singular sites are described as the historical king, but only the first of the three is historical and the other two are generic court references.
findings.grounds: 25:1 reads אַנְשֵׁ֤י חִזְקִיָּ֬ה מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה, a named ruler, while 25:5 carries לִפְנֵי מֶ֑לֶךְ and 25:6 the byte-identical לִפְנֵי מֶ֑לֶךְ, both generic; all three runs are byte tier at their cited refs. The distinction the row's warrant actually needs is number, plural at 25:2 and 25:3 against singular at 25:1, 25:5 and 25:6, and that distinction is byte-true and untouched, so the defect is the descriptor and the cluster warrant is unaffected. Both edges re-checked: 25:1|25:2 shares zero skeleton tokens and 25:3|25:4 shares zero skeleton tokens, so no undisclosed device straddles either edge.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the historical-king descriptor with a number-based one in boundary_rationale: the singular of the same lexeme at Prov.25.1, Prov.25.5 and Prov.25.6 against the plural bounded to this row's two verses. No other field changes. Proposal only.

findings.class: cross-seam echo disclosed but not weighed
findings.claim: The row's back seam carries the densest adjacent-verse token link in the surrounding run, and the disclosure names the echo without the boundedness digits that are what actually decide the seam in the row's favour.
findings.grounds: Both sides of the 25:5|25:6 seam, byte tier: 25:5 closes וְיִכּ֖וֹן בַּצֶּ֣דֶק כִּסְאֽוֹ and 25:6 opens אַל תִּתְהַדַּ֥ר לִפְנֵי מֶ֑לֶךְ. At skeleton tier that seam shares two tokens while the row's own internal link at 25:4|25:5 shares one and the following row's internal link at 25:6|25:7 shares one, so the cut severs the window's densest adjacent link. The deciding object is boundedness rather than density, and the row's object wins on it: the verse-initial verb, byte-identical at הָג֣וֹ and הָג֣וֹ, is returned by a contiguous skeleton sweep at 4 of 915 verses, of which Prov.16.33 and Prov.18.18 are contained-substring hits inside the lot-noun (הַגּוֹרָ֑ל and הַגּוֹרָ֑ל), leaving the verb at exactly 2 verses book-wide, both verse-initial and both inside this row; whereas the echoed phrase's preposition stands at 20 of 915 verses (6 of them inside Prov.25.1-Prov.27.27, at Prov.25.5, Prov.25.6, Prov.25.7, Prov.25.26, Prov.27.4, Prov.27.19) and its noun at an upper bound of 24 verses, that contiguous-skeleton figure itself carrying contained-substring hits such as גְמָלְךָ֣ at Prov.3.30, and the preposition recurs a third consecutive time at 25:7 in לִפְנֵ֣י נָדִ֑יב, so the phrase spans three consecutive verses and cannot bound any two-verse unit. The cut is right; the disclosure is under-argued.
findings.proposed_change: Extend the cross-seam disclosure in device_notes with the digits that decide it: the verse-initial verb at exactly 2 verses book-wide once the two contained-substring hits at Prov.16.33 and Prov.18.18 are excluded, against the echoed preposition at 20 verses book-wide and recurring at Prov.25.5, Prov.25.6 and Prov.25.7 consecutively. Span unchanged. Proposal only.

findings.class: work-unit scoping and governance citation in row prose
findings.claim: Two register rules are breached in row prose: the exclusivity digit is scoped to a writer part, and the cross-seam disclosure cites the campaign's own cohesion rule rather than the text.
findings.grounds: The phrases scoping the token to nowhere else in this part and to only these two sites in the part bind a corpus digit to a work unit invisible to a reader of the corpus, and the clause disclosing the echo per the standing cohesion rule cites governance rather than evidence; the register purge bars workflow, positional, tooling and governance language from row prose without exception, while what the cohesion rule requires is the disclosure itself, which the row does make. Corpus-scoped the claim is true and stronger than stated: the verse-initial verb הָג֣וֹ at 25:4 and the byte-identical הָג֣וֹ at 25:5 stand at exactly 2 of 915 verses once the lot-noun hits at Prov.16.33 and Prov.18.18 are excluded.
findings.proposed_change: Restate both digits in corpus terms (2 of 915 verses book-wide for the verse-initial verb, the four-verse contiguous sweep reduced by the two contained-substring hits) and delete the rule citation from device_notes, keeping the disclosure itself. No other field changes. Proposal only.

findings.class: unit_type against the campaign's own ruled test
findings.claim: The span is a bare double vetitive followed by its motive clause, the shape this campaign types admonition_unit, yet it ships as proverb_cluster with the form never tested and no deviation disclosure.
findings.grounds: 25:6 carries two vetitives at byte tier, אַל תִּתְהַדַּ֥ר opening the verse and אַֽל תַּעֲמֹֽד closing it, and 25:7 opens with the motive pair כִּ֤י ט֥וֹב. The ratified amendment records the decision-local precedent that a bare vetitive governs its verse as admonition_unit even inside the sentence collections, keyed to Prov.22.28 (אַל תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם), and the same prohibition-plus-motive shape is typed admonition_unit by the shipped rows at Prov.24.1-Prov.24.2 and Prov.24.21-Prov.24.22; the three sibling rows in this slice each run the test explicitly and record why their spans fall outside it, so the test is the campaign's own and is simply not run here. Re-swept at skeleton tier, the contiguous vetitive shape stands at 64 of 915 verses and is present at 25:6 and again at 25:8 and 25:9 beyond the row's back seam, so the surrounding material is admonition-shaped rather than sentence-shaped. Because the precedent is recorded as decision-local, this is adjudication input and not a settled violation; the span itself is not challenged, its two verses sharing a skeleton token across the seam and the second verse opening with a dependent motive particle.
findings.proposed_change: Retype unit_type and literature_type_guess from proverb_cluster to admonition_unit and add the one-sentence deviation disclosure that the collection's operative category is single_proverb with proverb_cluster its ruled multi-verse alternative; or, if the adjudicator keeps proverb_cluster, add the one sentence stating why a governing vetitive pair with its motive clause does not carry this span into admonition_unit. Either way the dependent fields re-open per the driver-swap rule -- observed_substrate_signals, device_notes, strongest_rejected_alternative and confidence. span, parent_collection and boundary_evidence_refs are unchanged. Proposal only; applied to nothing.

findings.class: mixed-tier splices and unqualified position claims
findings.claim: Four quoted claims are imprecise: two phrases put a byte-tier pointed word and an unpointed skeleton word inside one ref-bound phrase, and two closing-with claims read as verse-final when they hold only of the first colon.
findings.grounds: The row writes a pointed preposition ref-bound to 25:7 followed by an unpointed noun, and a pointed preposition ref-bound to 25:5 followed by an unpointed noun, whereas the source runs are לִפְנֵ֣י נָדִ֑יב at 25:7 and לִפְנֵי מֶ֑לֶךְ at 25:5, both byte tier at their refs, so the tier is mixed inside a single quoted phrase and is nowhere named. As to position, 25:6 does not close with the preposition -- its final word is תַּעֲמֹֽד -- and 25:5's final word is כִּסְאֽוֹ; the phrase לִפְנֵי מֶ֑לֶךְ closes only the first colon of each verse, the atnach standing on מֶ֑לֶךְ at 25:6 and on the byte-identical form at 25:5, so the claims are true of the colon and false of the verse as written.
findings.proposed_change: Re-cut the two phrases so both words come from the same tier and the tier is named, and qualify both position claims as first-colon rather than verse-final, citing the atnach placement. No other field changes. Proposal only.

findings.class: self-referential register, and both self-descriptions wrong
findings.claim: The row prose cites the campaign's cohesion rule and describes the decision record rather than the text, and both self-descriptions mis-state the row's own seams.
findings.grounds: The clause disclosing an unadopted cross-seam echo per the standing cohesion rule cites governance rather than evidence; the clause saying the row is bounded at 25.6 describes the record and mis-states the span, which is Prov.25.6-Prov.25.7 and is bounded at 25:5|25:6 in front and 25:7|25:8 behind; and the signal saying the preposition recurs at each seam is false at the back seam, since 25:7 carries לִפְנֵ֣י but 25:8 opens אַל תֵּצֵ֥א לָרִ֗ב מַ֫הֵ֥ר and carries none, 25:7 and 25:8 sharing zero skeleton tokens, so the preposition recurs across the front seam only, spanning 25:5, 25:6 and 25:7 consecutively.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the rule citation and the self-referential clause from device_notes and observed_substrate_signals, and restate the recurrence verse-anchored: the preposition stands at Prov.25.5, Prov.25.6 and Prov.25.7 consecutively and is absent from Prov.25.8, so it crosses the front seam only. No other field changes. Proposal only.
